markdown:
## The Location Landscape

Workplace flexibility has become a primary factor in job selection. Your policy position directly impacts your ability to attract and retain talent.

### The Candidate View

Survey data reveals:

- 65% prefer hybrid arrangements
- 25% prefer fully remote
- 10% prefer full-time office
- Flexibility is often non-negotiable for top talent

### Policy Options

Models in practice:

- Full remote (any location)
- Remote-first (office optional)
- Hybrid (2-3 days in office)
- Office-first (occasional remote)
- Full office (required presence)

### Compensation Implications

Location-based adjustments:

Have questions about your hiring strategy?

Book a free 30-minute consultation with our team. No commitment, just practical advice.

- Geographic pay differentials
- Remote work stipends
- Relocation packages
- Office commute benefits

### Hiring Strategy Alignment

Match policy to needs:

- Remote expands talent pool dramatically
- On-site requirements limit geography
- Hybrid requires local candidates
- Clear communication prevents surprises

### Role-Specific Considerations

Not one-size-fits-all:

- Some roles require presence
- Others fully remote-capable
- Team dynamics matter
- Client expectations factor in

### Honest Positioning

Attract the right candidates:

- State policy clearly in postings
- Discuss expectations early
- Be specific about flexibility
- Avoid bait-and-switch

### Future Proofing

Plan for evolution:

- Policy may change
- Employee preferences shift
- Competitive pressures mount
- Technology enables new models

### The TaaS Approach

We clearly communicate your workplace policy to candidates, ensuring only those aligned with your model advance.

Your location policy is a talent strategy decision, not just an operations choice.
